blocks.text: It’s time for The Weekend Read — Deadline’s curated collection of the long-form stories you might have missed this week.

First off, we have a deep dive into Netflix’s evolution from network television’s foe into a lifesaving friend. Then there’s a long look into a new report that reveals podcaster Joe Rogan is the must trusted man in media by almost half of the men surveyed, and why that might be…

We sat down with Florian Zeller, the Oscar-winning filmmaker behind The Father , to discuss why he wrote his latest film Bunker with real-life couple Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem in mind, and how they navigated playing out a huge argument on screen. And from our columnist Baz Bamigboye, a tribute to legendary British agent Jeremy Conway with a little help from Conway’s longtime client Helena Bonham-Carter.
And last but not least, director Daniel Chong takes us inside the making of his Pixar movie Hoppers .
Click on the list below to find out more.

How Netflix Evolved From Foe To Friend For Broadcast TV Image Credit: Disney/CBS/NBC/Fox Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix , have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for new season launches on broadcast — and beyond. The latest example is the major film and TV licensing deal Netflix recently made with Disney. It includes multi-year agreements for drama Will Trent and comedy Shifting Gears , whose existing seasons are launching on the streamer weeks ahead of their upcoming season premieres on ABC. The former debuted on Netflix earlier this month and is projected to crack the Nielsen Top 10 when the next ranking is released. Rea d the full article here

blocks.text: Do You Trust Joe Rogan? Image Credit: Getty A month after the former Fear Factor host inked a more than $200 million multi-year contract extension with Spotify for the Joe Rogan Experience, a just released report says Rogan is the most trusted figure in media by almost half the men surveyed. In the fractured media environment of 2026, a stunning 49% of men to be exact. Adding to the texture of that result is a deeper dive that one-time MAGA kingmaker Rogan is considered the Walter Cronkite of our age by 41% of Democrats in the Beyond The Manosphere study from Precision Strategies and Tunnl Data. While Rogan tops the trust list, he is closely followed by Stephen A. Smith (38%) among the 3,001 men Precision, which was founded in 2015 by ex-Democratic operative and White House aide Stephanie Cutter, and Tunnl surveyed last month. Breaking down the pre-midterms data further, potential POTUS candidate and Donald Trump dining companion Smith is trailed as an info source by The Charlie Kirk Show , fellow ESPNer Pat McAfee, Ben Shapiro and ex-Fox News top dog Tucker Carlson . blocks.text: Why Florian Zeller Wrote ‘Bunker’ For Penélope Cruz And Javier Bardem Image Credit: Josh Telles/Deadline Speaking over Zoom from his home in Paris, Florian Zeller says he could write poems all about Penélope Cruz. Instead, he wrote a thrilling movie called Bunker for her, and her husband, Javier Bardem . Zeller, the playwright, screenwriter and screen and stage director behind The Father (for which Anthony Hopkins won his second Best Actor Oscar) and plays that have run on Broadway and in London’s West End, emphasizes that he wasn’t interested in Cruz’s radiant beauty. “Of course she’s beautiful,” he says, but, “somehow we don’t care.” What do you mean? I ask. “Of course, she is talented, but she has something more, something unique, and it has to do with the fact that she’s always working with who she is. She’s always working with her deep emotions, and that in my experience is really rare.” Read the full interview here

Remembering Legendary British Agent Jeremy Conway Image Credit: Courtesy CVGG. Jeremy Conway — an artiste’s agent, and a titan of the industry with an unerring eye for the stars of the future — died earlier this month aged 87. His client list was legendary, a rollcall that included Anthony Hopkins , Brian Cox, Helena Bonham Carter , Benedict Cumberbatch, Claire Bloom, Greta Scacchi, Noma Dumezweni, Joanne Froggatt, and David Harewood Over 50 years ago, Conway founded his eponymous agency. In 1980, Nicki Van Gelder joined him, adding her name to the shingle. There were just three of them in the office then, and when John Grant joined in 1994 there were nine. “We are now 32!” Grant recently told Deadline of the company that’s now a powerhouse called Conway Van Gelder Grant . Grant confirmed that Conway — “his friend and mentor” — had died on 1 November this year. Conway was CVGG’s principal partner until he retired in 2015. In a tribute penned for Deadline, Bonham Carter, who’s still with the agency, recalled a note she had written for Conway’s retirement party thanking him “for my career.” She meant it. She continued, “I don’t think any of it would have happened if it weren’t for him. He started it all; 42 years ago, I was 17 and sitting in Jeremy’s office on a rather low futon or sofa watching him pace up and down in front of me in mild frustration. He had seen me in a Channel 4 drama playing an Edwardian ghost [1983’s A Pattern of Roses ] and was convinced I had something. I wasn’t so sure. I thought I should go to university. ‘Look,’ he said somewhat impatiently. ‘I really am one of the top five agents in London.’ And so began one of my longest partnerships in my life. We did, I think about 20 years together. And I never did go to university. And nor did I ever train.” Read the full tribute here

blocks.text: Inside The Making Of ‘Hoppers’ Image Credit: Disney/Pixar Daniel Chong cannot stop working with animals. His storyboarding credits span Toy Story shorts, Cars 2 , Dr. Seuss’s The Lorax and Inside Out , to name a few, but his first creator credit came with Cartoon Network’s Emmy-nominated We Bare Bears . As an Asian American creative in the industry, Chong explored social anxieties, friendship, assimilation, self-care and belonging through three bear brothers’ attempts to fit into human society. Now back at Pixar as a director, he brings those sensibilities to his first theatrical feature, Hoppers , and punches them up several notches. With environmentalism at its center, the film follows animal lover Mabel Tanaka ( Piper Curda ) as she tries to rehabilitate a local glade that was special to her and her late grandmother. To succeed, Mabel transfers her consciousness into an animatronic beaver and goes undercover in the animal world. Then all beaver dams break loose. The deeper Mabel goes, the more she uncovers the dynamics of the natural world, including those shaped by the pond’s ruler, Prince George ( Bobby Moynihan ), which causes her simple plan to save the glade to go awry.
